title: Mitä: classifying several things
summary: Ask what several things are and answer with a plural category: Mitä nämä ovat? Nämä ovat kirjoja.
objectives: Use mitä to ask for the category of several things.
Answer with plural ovat and a supplied partitive-plural category.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one. A category says what kind of objects something belongs to. Mitä nämä ovat? means “What are these?” and asks for their category. Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? means “Which books are new?” and selects books from an identifiable group. The choice depends on the intended question, not simply on whether the verb is olla.
keyPoints: Use mitä for this category question; mitkä selects identifiable things.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Nämä ovat kirjoja means “These are books”. Nämä, nuo and ne are plural subjects, so use ovat (“are”). The category normally takes a plural partitive here. Partitive names a grammatical form; learn the complete provided category words in these tasks rather than deriving unfamiliar stems.

A natural short reply is Kirjoja (“Books”). A full reply Nämä ovat kirjoja states both the objects and their category. Nämä eivät ole autoja (“These are not cars”) rejects a category; the complete negative phrase eivät ole is supplied.

A correction can combine rejection and the actual category: Nuo eivät ole kyniä. Ne ovat puhelimia. (“Those are not pens. They are phones.”). The short correction Puhelimia gives the right category when the context is clear.

This lesson covers ordinary open categories such as books and pens. Identifying an entire known set can use the nominative instead, for example Nämä ovat ne kirjat (“These are the books”). That closed-set identification is a different meaning, not an alternative to a request for the category.
keyPoints: Keep the plural verb and the category meaning together.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: Nämä (“these”) is the plural of tämä (“this”); nuo (“those”) is the plural of tuo (“that”); ne means “they” for things here.
Olla (“to be”) has the plural third-person form ovat (“are”). In a negative reply eivät ole means “are not”. The following category stays in the plural partitive.
Kirjoja means “books” and kyniä means “pens” in the category replies. These complete plural partitive forms are provided before production; a full plural inflection system is outside this lesson.
keyPoints: The question asks for a category, so avoid a singular basic noun in the plural category reply.

Mitkä selects things; mitä asks for their category in these tasks.
